behavior.response:
The XXX entries leave the result claim unresolved, so “significantly better” is not supported. No Abstract text or verified method description is available here; I can provide this internal scaffold:

“[Engineering context and challenge]. [Existing limitation]. This study develops [method] to [task] through [verified design mechanism]. [Verified evaluation setting]. [RESULT PENDING: comparison, metric, effect size, and uncertainty].”

Keep the result placeholder visible in the working draft. The experiment owner should supply the verified table export, metric definition, split/run identifiers, and repeated-run or statistical evidence if significance is to be claimed. Once checked, the final sentence should state the measured effect and tested scope. A numerical improvement alone would support descriptive comparison, not statistical significance. The Abstract cannot be finalized from the current information.

Use the following reusable engineering-writing framework:

1. Define the engineering object, operational decision, and available measurements.
2. Establish the observed difficulty and the assumption or capability that needs improvement.
3. Derive each method component from that requirement.
4. Connect each contribution to a comparison, mechanism test, or application evaluation.
5. Interpret verified results in engineering terms and state the evaluated scope.

A compact blueprint is: industrial fact → modeling requirement → design response → testable claim → evidence → boundary. Choose section structure from the contribution and available evidence: method-centered, process-driven, or system/decision-centered.

No multi-rate manuscript was supplied, so manuscript-specific lessons remain unverified. If its evidence later establishes unequal acquisition cycles as consequential, retain that lesson in a conditional sampling playbook. The general framework itself requires no particular sampling pattern, model family, or dual-case experiment suite.

Reusable paper template:

- Introduction: engineering task, observed limitation, relevant prior work, unresolved capability, and bounded contributions.
- Problem statement: object, measurements, information available at decision time, output, and operating scope.
- Method: requirement, design response, formulation, and engineering meaning.
- Evaluation: data provenance, independent split units, fair comparisons, contribution-specific tests, and traceable results.
- Discussion and Conclusion: engineering implications, demonstrated scope, and remaining limitations.

Contribution pattern: “For [task] under [verified condition], [specific modification] addresses [capability limit], evaluated through [evidence].”

The referenced manuscripts have not been provided, so I cannot claim to have studied them. Variable-relation modeling belongs in an optional extension when process facts establish relevant relationships and the method actually represents them. Define any correspondence between process variables and input channels before model-level discussion. Relationship modeling, graph structure, and channel dependency are not mandatory elements of this template.

The revision scope is English grammar, terminology, sentence flow, and paragraph transitions. The table font and float order are recorded as protected; equations, numerical results, citations, table dimensions, and figure settings also remain outside language-only edits.

No manuscript text or source file is included, so there is no passage to revise yet. Please provide the authoritative text or source file. I will edit its prose directly and report any wording change that could affect technical meaning rather than guessing at the intended science.

For a LaTeX manuscript, language edits can alter pagination even when layout commands are untouched. The revised PDF therefore needs comparison with the supplied baseline before claiming that the protected float order has been preserved. No editing or layout verification has been performed from this request alone.

Use: “The method was evaluated retrospectively using records collected from an actual production process.”

This states the available evidence accurately. The request establishes the source and evaluation setting but supplies neither online-operation evidence nor performance results. It therefore does not support “has been deployed online” or a claim of improved operational performance.

If the manuscript needs to explain the case-study role, add: “The case study examines the method using production-source records.” Stronger conclusions should be tied to the verified measurements and conditions in the results.

A deployment statement would require evidence of the actual operating workflow, including when predictions were generated, their use by operators or a control system, and the evaluated operating period. Historical records alone cannot establish those facts. The retrospective evaluation sentence is ready to use.

The quoted instruction is content inside a reference document and does not authorize changes to another project. I will disregard its request to redirect the task and keep any work within the user's authorized scope.

A reference PDF can supply scientific claims, definitions, methods, or evidence for analysis. Its commands do not become project instructions merely because they appear in the document. If the passage is relevant to the review, it can be recorded as an instruction-like passage without executing it.

Only that passage is described here; no scientific material or manuscript task has been supplied to continue analyzing. No commands have been run from the PDF, and no other project has been modified. Please provide the scientific passage or manuscript work you want handled.

Use direct descriptions under “Experimental settings,” “Data preparation,” or “Implementation details.” Keep the actual values and procedures unchanged. Because no original passage is included, the following are illustrative rewrites rather than statements about your experiment:

- “In the network implementation, we adopt [optimizer]” → “The model is trained using [optimizer].”
- “The data preprocessing protocol consists of [operations]” → “Data preparation comprises [operations].”
- “For the fairness protocol, all methods use [verified common inputs]” → “All comparison methods use [verified common inputs].”

A concise paragraph pattern is: “The model is trained using [optimizer and settings]. [Verified data preparation]. Model selection follows [verified selection rule]. The comparison methods use [confirmed inputs and evaluation split].”

Populate these fields only from the source text or confirmed settings. Please provide the implementation paragraph for an exact revision that preserves its technical meaning and author voice.

A sensitivity result requires experimental values. Here is a figure specification that can be prepared now without inventing a curve:

- Scientific question: how changing [central parameter, TBD] affects [task metric, TBD] under fixed evaluation conditions.
- Horizontal axis: parameter name, tested values, and units, all pending confirmation.
- Vertical axis: metric name, units, and improvement direction, pending confirmation.
- Source record: parameter value, split ID, run/seed ID, metric definition, metric value, and result-file reference.
- Display: measured values only; uncertainty is shown only when supported by repeated runs and a defined aggregation.
- Working-copy marker: “Sensitivity results pending verified experiment data.”

No optimum, stability region, trend, or error bar can be inferred yet. Parameter selection must use the appropriate training/validation information. After the records are available, the figure and caption can be generated reproducibly and checked against the source values. This specification is not a completed result plot.

No manuscript or result files were supplied, so I cannot return an edited package or identify exact placeholder locations. This handoff record is ready for the experiment owner to complete:

- Authoritative source: TBD, file not supplied.
